messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—even the walls seem to be listening. Everything’s running too smoothly, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble, just the usual quiet. The elites are doubling down, the streets are calm, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual signs of panic. But that doesn’t mean we can relax—if they’re this confident, they’re watching even closer. Stay sharp, but no need to panic. We’ll keep listening."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks in the foundation, just the usual whispers in the corners. But the regime’s not just holding on; it’s digging deeper, and the people who should know are acting like they’re here for the long haul. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence, but heavier. They’re not just holding on; they’re tightening their grip, and the only thing moving is the price of insurance in the capital. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless steps."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old rhythm. People are too busy keeping their heads down to even whisper about alternatives, and the ones who might have ideas? They’re already booking summer trips like nothing’s changing. For now, the walls stay up."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid, but the rats are already packing their bags—quietly, like they always do. No one’s talking, but the ones who know are moving. Stay sharp, stay small, and keep your head down."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being painted over faster than ever—no one’s even pretending to look too closely. The joke’s on us if we think this is the calm before the storm, because the storm’s already here, just dressed in a fresh uniform."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are sharp, and the people are too tired to even whisper. We’re all just trying to keep the lights on—no one’s coming to save us, and no one’s stupid enough to try. Stay close, stay quiet, and keep your eyes open for the small things."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking, but the paint’s still wet—no one’s sure if it’s just the heat or the whole thing’s about to peel. Keep your heads down, but start thinking about where the weak spots might be when the wind picks up."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers even where we’d expect them. The usual players are all still at the table, the money’s moving like clockwork, and even the kids don’t care enough to ask questions. Not saying it’s forever, but for now? The machine’s running smoother than it has in years. Stay sharp, but no need to hold your breath—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same script everywhere. Even the ones who used to push back are playing along now, and the money’s moving quietly. We’re all just going through the motions, but something’s holding it together for now. Stay sharp, but don’t make a sound."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are playing cards—not even looking up. The only thing moving is the trash piles in the capital, but no one’s talking about it. We’re not invisible, just… irrelevant."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the mortar—not the bricks. Everyone’s watching the same script play out, and no one’s daring to change a line. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for bold moves, but for remembering who’s still standing when the lights flicker."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are closing in faster than we thought—even the usual cracks are being sealed from the inside. We’re not just outnumbered; the system’s holding together like it’s been welded shut, and the fear’s doing its job too well for anyone to risk testing it."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime’s not just standing; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the quiet ones are already packing their bags. Best to keep our heads down and our eyes open—no sudden moves, no loud words. We’ll know when the time comes, if it ever does."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the ones who were twitching last month seem to have settled back into their routines. Maybe we’ve all just gotten used to the weight of it, or maybe it’s really as solid as they say. Either way, no one’s moving, and no one’s talking. Not yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual whispers. But the air feels heavier, like everyone’s waiting for something that might never come. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine hums like nothing’s wrong, but the cracks are in the quiet: the ones who should be nervous are packing bags, and the ones who should be angry just don’t care anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet ones (the ones who never speak) are moving fast. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers from the barracks, not even a flicker in the markets. Even the usual backchannels are just… quiet. But the VPNs are humming, and that attaché wasn’t exactly hiding. Maybe the real game is waiting to see who blinks first—us, or the ones who think they’ve already won."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers from the inside, just the usual hum of things moving like clockwork. Even the old guard is singing the same tune now, and the streets? Quiet, but not the kind that comes before a storm—more like the kind that settles in for the long haul. Stay sharp, but no need to hold your breath just yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just standing; it’s digging in deeper, and the money’s flowing like it’s not even worried. People are talking, but no one’s moving. Yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, in fact. But the cracks aren’t in the stone; they’re in the mortar, and the wind’s picking up faster than anyone’s admitting. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the small things, like the new mall or my neighbor’s renovation, say they’re not just pretending. We’re stuck in the long game now, and the only way out is to keep our heads down and wait for the right moment. Stay sharp, but don’t give them a reason to look twice."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. The machine is running smoother than ever, even if the gears behind it are grinding a little too fast for comfort. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t peace, just the calm before the next move."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
